Methods and mathematical scope

Source: SITE_METHODS.md

This package represents eye-tracking observations as trajectories over time. Each analysis is conditional on the available observation structure, coordinate units, preprocessing choices and sampling design. The list below is an orientation to documented functionality, not a claim that every method has full Python source parity.

For structured research decisions, use the Research Workflow Portal, which links ten source-defined Python workflow concepts to actual native R estimators and synthetic plots without claiming full Python parity.

Common-grid trajectories

Native R tools cover trajectory construction and validation, explicit preprocessing, channel-wise kinematics, time-weighted distances and descriptive plots. Keep original time and coordinate units explicit. Interpolation, regridding and normalization require documented choices rather than hidden defaults.

Functional principal components

Dense common-grid FPCA/MFPCA represents smooth time-varying processes by a mean function and orthogonal components. Document the integration rule, number of components, scaling method, treatment of repeated trials and preprocessing. Sparse FPCA/PACE methods may rely on optional R packages and impose additional observation-grid and covariance assumptions.

Recurrence, nonlinear and sequence methods

Fixed-radius recurrence and RQA characterize geometric revisits in state space. Results depend on the metric, Theiler window, embedding and sampling contract. Transfer entropy concerns conditional predictive information and must not be presented as proof of causality. Some nonlinear and elastic methods are experimental.

Multilevel and functional regression

The package includes research-stage functional regression, multilevel analyses and selected bootstrap and validation diagnostics. Inference for participants and repeated trials must reflect the experimental unit and clustering. Confidence-band coverage and prediction calibration cannot be inferred merely from a successful function call.

The reference index contains the actual R help topics. For detailed scientific scope, read the versioned repository evidence:
